run.procedureSummary: Every cycle (1-5) runs five passes, and each pass finishes across all six tiers before the next one starts. (1) Load: add the cycle's new chunks to each tier. No trimming yet, so a tier can sit over budget. (2) Evict: go through tiers 1 to 6 in order. If a tier holds more than its budget, cut it back to budget and add the excess to the next tier out, before that tier is checked. Excess from tier 6 is dropped. (3) Flag: use the post-evict counts. A COLD tier at or above its HOT mark becomes HOT. A HOT tier at or below its COLD mark becomes COLD. A tier between the marks keeps its flag. Every flip is logged. (4) Rebalance: use the post-flag counts and work out all six amounts first. A COLD tier loses floor(n/4), which is dropped. A HOT tier loses floor(n/2), which goes to the tier one closer to the LLM (tier k-1). Tier 1's promotion is dropped. Then apply all six at once. Over-budget tiers are left alone until the next cycle's evict, and after cycle 5 they stay as they are. (5) Reset check: if the stack total is over 38, every tier becomes floor(n/2) and the removed chunks are dropped. A total of exactly 38 does not reset. One running drop tally covers tier-6 evictions, compactions, tier-1 promotions and resets.

openPoints.point: What 'anything over budget moves out' means in Evict
openPoints.assumption: Only the excess above budget moves. The tier is left holding exactly its budget.

openPoints.point: Which counts the Flag step uses
openPoints.assumption: The post-evict counts of the same cycle. Flags carry over between cycles, and every tier starts COLD.

openPoints.point: Whether a promotion can push a tier over budget, or be cascaded on, within the same cycle
openPoints.assumption: No. All six amounts are worked out from the post-flag counts and applied together. A promotion into a tier does not change what that tier compacts or promotes.
No. A reset only halves the holdings, and flags are re-evaluated at the next cycle's Flag step.
Each tier keeps floor(n/2). The dropped amount is n - floor(n/2), so an odd tier drops the larger half.

openPoints.point: Whether a reset can follow the cycle 5 rebalance
openPoints.assumption: Yes, the reset check runs in cycle 5 as normal. The total was exactly 38, so it did not fire.
